chapters.title_uz: Milliy iqtisodiyot va uning makroiqtisodiy ko'rsatkichlari
chapters.title_ru: Национальная экономика и её макроэкономические показатели
chapters.title_en: National economy and its macroeconomic indicators

questions.text_en: Which of the following represents the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders during a specific period?
questions.explanation_en: GDP is the standard measure of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders. NNI includes net foreign income, and national income is broader than GDP after adjustments.

questions.text_en: What is the key difference between GDP and GNP?
options: GNP includes net income from abroad
options_ru: ВНП включает чистый доход из-за границы
options_en: GNP includes net income from abroad
questions.explanation_en: GNP includes income earned by nationals from abroad, while GDP measures production only within borders. This accounts for foreign income flows that GDP excludes.

questions.text_en: Which measurement removes depreciation of capital stock from GDP?
questions.explanation_en: NDP equals GDP minus depreciation of capital stock, providing a more accurate measure of sustainable income. NNP further adjusts for net foreign income.

questions.text_en: GDP per capita is calculated by dividing total GDP by what variable?
questions.explanation_en: GDP per capita divides total GDP by population to measure average economic output per person. This indicates living standards and productivity per capita.

questions.text_en: Which economic indicator measures the average price level of goods and services?
questions.explanation_en: The GDP deflator measures price level changes of all goods and services produced. It's essential for converting nominal GDP to real GDP.

questions.text_en: In national accounting, consumption (C) typically includes which type of spending?
options: Household purchases of goods and services
options_en: Household purchases of goods and services
questions.explanation_en: Consumption represents household spending on goods and services. Business capital spending is investment, and government salary is part of government spending.

questions.text_en: What does investment (I) in macroeconomics primarily include?
options: Formation of fixed capital and inventory
options_en: Formation of fixed capital and inventory
questions.explanation_en: Macroeconomic investment includes business fixed capital formation and inventory changes. Stock purchases are financial investments, not productive investment.

questions.text_en: Which of the following is NOT typically included in GDP calculations?
questions.explanation_en: Non-market household services like cooking and childcare are excluded from GDP. Market services, infrastructure, agriculture, and manufacturing are all included.

questions.text_en: The expenditure approach to measuring GDP includes all of the following except:
questions.explanation_en: The expenditure approach uses C+I+G+(X-M). Primary production factors like labor and capital are not direct GDP components in this approach but determine output.

questions.text_en: Which indicator specifically measures economic performance in relation to environmental sustainability?
questions.explanation_en: Green GDP adjusts GDP for environmental degradation and resource depletion. Traditional GDP doesn't account for environmental costs or sustainability.

questions.text_en: Which of the following characterizes the primary sector of an economy?
options_ru: Сельское хозяйство и добыча природных ресурсов
questions.explanation_en: The primary sector includes agriculture, mining, and forestry. Secondary is manufacturing, tertiary is services, and quaternary involves knowledge-based activities.

questions.text_en: Real GDP differs from nominal GDP primarily in that it:
questions.explanation_en: Real GDP is adjusted for inflation using a price deflator, showing actual economic growth independent of price changes. Nominal GDP uses current prices.

questions.text_en: Which of the following would reduce a country's national income compared to its GDP?
options: Income earned by foreign nationals from abroad
Net payments made to foreign nationals for factor services
options_ru: Чистые платежи иностранным гражданам за услуги факторов
options_en: Income earned by foreign nationals from abroad
Net payments made to foreign nationals for factor services
questions.explanation_en: National income is reduced by net payments to foreigners for factor services. Foreign income earned domestically increases it, and export growth increases GDP.

questions.text_en: The production approach to GDP measurement focuses on which of the following?
options: Value added at each production stage
options_ru: Добавленная стоимость на каждом этапе производства
options_en: Value added at each production stage
questions.explanation_en: The production approach sums value added across all production stages to avoid double-counting. It measures the difference between output and intermediate inputs.

questions.text_en: Which indicator best reflects the material welfare of a population?
questions.explanation_en: GDP per capita measures average output per person, reflecting material welfare better than total GDP. A large economy with low per capita means unequal distribution.

questions.text_en: In national accounting, which component represents payments to individuals not related to current production?
questions.explanation_en: Transfer payments like pensions and welfare don't represent current production and are excluded from GDP. Wages, profit, rent, and interest are all factor incomes from production.

questions.text_en: Which measurement approach calculates GDP by summing all factor incomes?
questions.explanation_en: The income approach sums wages, profits, rents, and interest. The expenditure approach sums C+I+G+(X-M), while production approach uses value added.

questions.text_en: What would cause a divergence between nominal and real GDP growth rates?
questions.explanation_en: Price changes (inflation/deflation) cause divergence between nominal and real GDP. Productivity changes affect both similarly; consumption and investment changes are captured in both.

questions.text_en: Net National Product (NNP) is best defined as:
options_ru: Общий ВВП плюс доход из-за границы
Валовой внутренний продукт на душу населения
questions.explanation_en: NNP adjusts GNP by subtracting capital depreciation to show sustainable national income. It's narrower than GNP and broader than national disposable income.

questions.text_en: Which of the following is included in GDP but not in sustainable national income?
questions.explanation_en: GDP doesn't subtract environmental degradation costs, while sustainable income does. Manufacturing and services are included in both measures.

questions.text_en: An economy's economic structure is primarily analyzed by examining:
options: Sectoral distribution of output and employment
options_ru: Распределение выпуска и занятости по секторам
options_en: Sectoral distribution of output and employment
questions.explanation_en: Economic structure analysis examines sectoral composition (agriculture, industry, services). This reveals development stage and productivity patterns across the economy.

questions.text_en: Which indicator directly measures the average standard of living?
options_ru: Доход или потребление на душу населения
questions.explanation_en: Per capita income/consumption indicators directly measure average living standards. Total size measures economy scale, while exports measure trade capacity.

questions.text_en: The circular flow model of an economy shows that income paid for factors of production must equal which component?
questions.explanation_en: The circular flow shows that factor income equals total expenditure on output. This is the fundamental accounting identity in national income accounting.

questions.text_en: Which measurement converts nominal values using price indices?
questions.explanation_en: Real GDP uses price deflators to convert nominal to real values, removing inflation effects. This shows actual output growth independent of price level changes.

questions.text_en: In an open economy, which component of GDP measures economic interaction with the rest of the world?
questions.explanation_en: Net exports (exports minus imports) measure international trade and capital flows. It captures foreign demand for domestic goods and domestic demand for foreign goods.

questions.text_en: What is the primary limitation of using GDP as a welfare measure?
options: It fails to account for income distribution
options_en: It fails to account for income distribution
questions.explanation_en: GDP doesn't capture income inequality, so high GDP can mask low living standards for many. Environmental costs and non-market activities are also not reflected.

questions.text_en: Which national accounting identity holds that total output must equal:
options: Total income plus savings plus taxes
options_ru: Общий доход плюс сбережения плюс налоги
options_en: Total income plus savings plus taxes
questions.explanation_en: The income-expenditure identity shows that all income is either consumed or saved, and taxes are paid from income. Total output equals total income in a closed system.

questions.text_en: Economic indicators like GDP, inflation rate, and unemployment rate are primarily used to:
options: Monitor macroeconomic health and guide policy
options_ru: Отслеживать макроэкономическое здоровье и направлять политику
options_en: Monitor macroeconomic health and guide policy
questions.explanation_en: Macroeconomic indicators track overall economic performance and inform government policy decisions. They reveal economy-wide trends, not individual or sectoral outcomes.

chapters.title_uz: Iqtisodiy rivojlanish, iqtisodiy o'sish va milliy boy
chapters.title_ru: Экономическое развитие, экономический рост и национальное богатство
chapters.title_en: Economic Development, Economic Growth and National Wealth

questions.text_en: Economic growth is best defined as which of the following?
options: An increase in real per capita output
options_ru: Увеличение реального объема выпуска на душу населения
options_en: An increase in real per capita output
questions.explanation_en: Economic growth measures increases in real per capita output, reflecting actual expansion in productive capacity. Price increases, government spending, and money supply don't represent true growth.

questions.text_en: Capital accumulation contributes to long-term economic growth primarily by:
options: Building productive capacity for future output
options_ru: Построение производственной способности для будущего выпуска
options_en: Building productive capacity for future output
questions.explanation_en: Capital accumulation increases productive capacity, enabling higher future output. While it may reduce current consumption, it's essential for sustained long-term growth.

questions.text_en: Human capital development affects economic growth by:
questions.explanation_en: Human capital improvements through education and training increase labor productivity and innovation capacity. Skilled workers contribute more to growth than supply reductions.

questions.text_en: Technological progress promotes economic growth by allowing:
options_ru: Больше выпуска из того же количества входов
questions.explanation_en: Technological progress increases productivity by enabling more output from the same inputs. This is a key driver of long-term growth independent of resource increases.

questions.text_en: National wealth accumulation is primarily driven by which factor?
questions.explanation_en: National wealth grows through savings channeled into productive capital formation. Consumption reduces wealth, transfers redistribute existing wealth, and population changes affect per capita measures.

questions.text_en: Which indicator best measures improvement in quality of life and development?
questions.explanation_en: HDI combines income, education, and health indicators to measure development comprehensively. GDP alone doesn't capture life quality; population size and budget don't indicate welfare.

questions.text_en: Sustainable development differs from traditional growth by emphasizing:
options_ru: Балансирование роста с защитой окружающей среды
questions.explanation_en: Sustainable development seeks growth that preserves environmental and social resources for future generations. It differs from both maximum immediate output and pure resource conservation.

questions.text_en: Infrastructure development contributes to economic growth by:
options: Enabling efficient movement of goods and services
options_ru: Обеспечение эффективного движения товаров и услуг
options_en: Enabling efficient movement of goods and services
questions.explanation_en: Good infrastructure reduces transaction costs and enables business efficiency. While infrastructure requires investment, its benefits exceed costs through productivity gains.

questions.text_en: Education investment affects long-term growth rates primarily through:
questions.explanation_en: Education builds human capital and innovation capacity, driving productivity growth. Effects are long-term; immediate GDP and price effects are secondary.

questions.text_en: Which factor is NOT typically considered a key driver of economic growth?
questions.explanation_en: Consumer debt is a financial flow, not a productive capacity creator. True growth drivers are innovation, capital investment, and human capital, which expand productive potential.

questions.text_en: Productivity growth is essential to economic growth because it:
options: Enables output growth independent of input increases
options_ru: Обеспечивает рост выпуска независимо от увеличения входов
options_en: Enables output growth independent of input increases
questions.explanation_en: Productivity allows more output from same resources, enabling growth without resource expansion limits. Price increases, employment reduction, and capital limits are separate issues.

questions.text_en: Which aspect of development emphasizes improvement in living conditions beyond income?
questions.explanation_en: Quality of life indicators (health, education, environment) measure development comprehensively. GDP growth alone doesn't ensure improvements in these welfare dimensions.

questions.text_en: Economic modernization primarily involves shifting from:
options: Agricultural to industrial and service sectors
options_ru: Сельскохозяйственного к промышленному и сервисному секторам
options_en: Agricultural to industrial and service sectors
questions.explanation_en: Modernization moves economies from agriculture through industrialization to services. This shift reflects technological progress and changing comparative advantages.

questions.text_en: The role of foreign direct investment in developing countries is primarily to:
questions.explanation_en: FDI brings capital, technology, and expertise to developing economies, supplementing domestic resources. While it complements rather than replaces savings, it can affect employment and policy.

questions.text_en: Long-term growth potential is most fundamentally limited by:
options: Available productive capacity and factor resources
options_ru: Доступная производственная способность и ресурсы факторов
options_en: Available productive capacity and factor resources
questions.explanation_en: Growth capacity depends on available capital, labor, technology, and natural resources. Budgets, consumption, and interest rates affect demand and allocation but not fundamental capacity.

questions.text_en: Which statement best describes the relationship between savings and growth?
options: Savings finance investment which drives growth
options_ru: Сбережения финансируют инвестиции, которые способствуют росту
options_en: Savings finance investment which drives growth
questions.explanation_en: Savings provide capital for productive investment, enabling future growth. While they require current consumption sacrifice, they're essential for growth and not guaranteed to eliminate poverty alone.

questions.text_en: Natural resources contribute to economic development through which mechanism?
options: Raw materials for production and export
options_en: Raw materials for production and export
questions.explanation_en: Natural resources provide inputs for production and export value. Resource wealth alone doesn't guarantee development; effective utilization and processing add value.

questions.text_en: Which indicator specifically measures a nation's wealth?
options: Accumulated stock of assets minus liabilities
options_en: Accumulated stock of assets minus liabilities
questions.explanation_en: National wealth represents accumulated capital stock (assets minus liabilities). Annual income (GDP) is a flow, different from the accumulated stock of wealth.

questions.text_en: The primary constraint on growth for developing economies is often:
questions.explanation_en: Developing economies lack sufficient capital and technology for rapid productivity growth. Excessive capital, foreign investment, and consumption are not primary constraints.

questions.text_en: Which strategy is most likely to achieve sustainable growth in a developing economy?
options: Investing in education, infrastructure, and technology
options_ru: Инвестирование в образование, инфраструктуру и технологию
options_en: Investing in education, infrastructure, and technology
questions.explanation_en: Balanced investment in human capital, infrastructure, and technology drives sustainable growth. Consumption maximization, population control alone, and minimal government don't ensure sustained development.

questions.text_en: Technological transfer from developed to developing countries primarily benefits growth through:
options: Access to proven production methods and innovations
options_ru: Доступ к проверенным методам производства и инновациям
options_en: Access to proven production methods and innovations
questions.explanation_en: Technology transfer accelerates development by providing access to advanced methods without full R&D costs. It affects employment patterns but doesn't inherently eliminate local capacity.

questions.text_en: The concept of convergence in development economics suggests that:
options: Developing countries grow faster, approaching developed levels
options_ru: Развивающиеся страны растут быстрее, приближаясь к развитым уровням
Темпы роста идентичны во всем мире
options_en: Developing countries grow faster, approaching developed levels
questions.explanation_en: Convergence theory predicts catch-up growth where developing nations grow faster than developed ones. However, this assumes access to technology and capital for catch-up.

questions.text_en: Institutional quality affects economic growth primarily through its impact on:
options: Property rights, contracts, and investment incentives
options_ru: Права собственности, контракты и инвестиционные стимулы
options_en: Property rights, contracts, and investment incentives
questions.explanation_en: Good institutions (rule of law, property rights, contract enforcement) create investment incentives. Poor institutions discourage productive investment despite potential returns.

questions.text_en: Which development indicator captures both income and non-income dimensions of welfare?
questions.explanation_en: HDI combines income, education, and health to comprehensively measure development. GDP alone ignores education and health; trade balance and unemployment are partial indicators.

questions.text_en: Endogenous growth theory emphasizes that growth is driven by:
options: Internal factors like knowledge and innovation
options_ru: Внутренние факторы, такие как знания и инновации
options_en: Internal factors like knowledge and innovation
questions.explanation_en: Endogenous growth theory shows that growth is internally generated through innovation and human capital accumulation, not just external resources.

questions.text_en: The role of research and development in economic growth is to:
questions.explanation_en: R&D creates innovations that increase productivity and enable growth. While it has temporary adjustment costs, the long-term productivity gains drive sustained growth.

questions.text_en: Which factor is least directly related to a country's development level?
questions.explanation_en: Stock prices reflect expectations about future profits but don't directly measure real development. Education, healthcare, and infrastructure directly affect productive capacity and living standards.

questions.text_en: The multiplier effect of development investments works by:
options: Initial spending generating additional income and spending rounds
options_ru: Начальные расходы, генерирующие дополнительные раунды доходов и расходов
options_en: Initial spending generating additional income and spending rounds
questions.explanation_en: The multiplier shows how initial investment income circulates through the economy, generating multiple rounds of spending and income. This amplifies growth impact beyond direct investment.

questions.text_en: The consumption function relates consumption to which primary variable?
questions.explanation_en: The consumption function shows how consumption varies with disposable income. Keynes established this fundamental relationship; prices, interest rates, and government spending have secondary effects.

questions.text_en: The marginal propensity to consume (MPC) is best defined as:
options: Change in consumption from a change in income
options_en: Change in consumption from a change in income
questions.explanation_en: MPC measures how much additional consumption results from additional income. It's the slope of the consumption function, not total consumption ratio.

questions.text_en: If the marginal propensity to consume is 0.8, what is the marginal propensity to save?
questions.explanation_en: MPC and MPS sum to 1.0, as income is either consumed or saved. If MPC = 0.8, then MPS = 0.2, meaning 20% of additional income is saved.

questions.text_en: Which of the following is an example of fixed capital investment?
questions.explanation_en: Fixed capital (factories, machinery, buildings) is productive real assets. Inventory is working capital; stocks and bonds are financial investments, not productive investment.

questions.text_en: Working capital refers to which type of investment?
options: Short-term assets like inventory and receivables
options_ru: Краткосрочные активы, такие как товарно-материальные ценности и дебиторская задолженность
options_en: Short-term assets like inventory and receivables
questions.explanation_en: Working capital represents short-term assets needed for daily operations (inventory, cash). Fixed capital is long-term; real estate and financial instruments are separate categories.

questions.text_en: The average propensity to consume is calculated as:
options: Total consumption divided by total income
Change in consumption divided by change in income
options_ru: Общее потребление, разделенное на общий доход
Изменение потребления, разделенное на изменение дохода
options_en: Total consumption divided by total income
Change in consumption divided by change in income
questions.explanation_en: APC = Total Consumption / Total Income. It shows the average proportion of income spent on consumption. MPC looks at changes, not total ratios.

questions.text_en: Which factor would most likely increase household savings rates?
options_ru: Более низкие процентные ставки на сбережения
questions.explanation_en: Increased current income raises savings through both higher available funds and confidence. Higher expected future income may reduce current savings; lower interest rates discourage saving.

questions.text_en: Business investment is primarily motivated by:
questions.explanation_en: Firms invest based on expected returns on investment (ROI). Consumer demand, subsidies, and labor costs are inputs into ROI calculations but not primary motivators alone.

questions.text_en: Capital formation is essential for economic growth because it:
options: Builds productive capacity for future output
options_ru: Строит производственную способность для будущего выпуска
options_en: Builds productive capacity for future output
questions.explanation_en: Capital formation expands productive capacity, enabling sustained growth. While it may affect employment and fiscal impacts, the key benefit is building future production capability.

questions.text_en: The relationship between savings rate and investment rate in a closed economy is:
questions.explanation_en: In a closed economy, savings must equal investment by the national accounting identity. In open economies, they can diverge through current account imbalances.

questions.text_en: Which investment factor best predicts long-term business profitability?
questions.explanation_en: Expected ROI on productive assets best predicts sustainable profitability. Stock volatility, interest rates, and sentiment are market factors but don't directly indicate productive returns.

questions.text_en: Consumption patterns differ between countries primarily due to:
questions.explanation_en: Consumption patterns reflect income levels and cultural preferences. Prices vary; utility functions differ across cultures; production costs don't determine consumption patterns.

questions.text_en: The income effect in consumption theory describes how:
options_ru: Изменения цены пропорционально влияют на спрос
Изменения дохода влияют на количество потребления
questions.explanation_en: The income effect shows how more income enables higher consumption of most goods. The substitution effect shows how relative price changes affect consumption choices.

questions.text_en: The multiplier effect of investment spending demonstrates that:
options: Initial investment generates multiple rounds of income
Multipliers are always less than one
options_ru: Начальные инвестиции генерируют несколько раундов доходов
options_en: Initial investment generates multiple rounds of income
Multipliers are always less than one
questions.explanation_en: The multiplier shows how initial investment income circulates through the economy, generating additional rounds of spending. Multipliers exceed 1.0 when MPC is positive.

questions.text_en: Why might households increase savings despite rising income levels?
questions.explanation_en: Precautionary saving increases with uncertainty about future income stability. Rising consumption desire, inflation reduction, and government spending would reduce savings.

questions.text_en: Which factor would most directly reduce the savings rate?
options: Higher inflation with constant nominal income
options_ru: Повышенная инфляция при постоянном номинальном доходе
options_en: Higher inflation with constant nominal income
questions.explanation_en: Inflation eroding purchasing power reduces real income and savings. Higher interest rates encourage saving; job security enables saving; tax credits for savers encourage saving.

questions.text_en: Investment in human capital (education and training) differs from physical capital in that it:
options: Is embodied in individuals and enhances productivity
options_ru: Не может быть амортизировано или заменено
Воплощено в людях и повышает производительность
options_en: Is embodied in individuals and enhances productivity
questions.explanation_en: Human capital investments build skills that increase productivity and worker earnings. Unlike physical capital, it's embodied in people and portable across employers.

questions.text_en: The paradox of thrift describes the situation where:
options: Individual saving reduces aggregate demand and national income
options_ru: Индивидуальное сбережение снижает совокупный спрос и национальный доход
options_en: Individual saving reduces aggregate demand and national income
questions.explanation_en: The paradox of thrift shows that while individual saving is beneficial, aggregate saving reduces demand and income. This can be resolved through investment offsetting saving.

questions.text_en: Credit and consumer debt affect consumption by:
options: Allowing consumption to exceed current income
options_en: Allowing consumption to exceed current income
questions.explanation_en: Consumer credit enables spending beyond current income but requires future repayment. While it smooths consumption, it increases future obligations and total interest costs.

questions.text_en: In the life-cycle hypothesis of consumption, individuals typically:
options: Consume most income in old age
options_ru: Ничего не экономят в рабочие годы
Потребляют большинство доходов в преклонном возрасте
options_en: Consume most income in old age
questions.explanation_en: The life-cycle hypothesis shows people save during working years to maintain consumption in retirement. This implies positive savings during peak earning years.

questions.text_en: Which investment generates the highest return on investment?
questions.explanation_en: Investment returns vary with risk and expected profitability. Higher risk investments offer potential for higher returns; government bonds are safe but offer lower returns.

questions.text_en: Depreciation in capital accounting represents:
options: Loss of capital value from wear and obsolescence
options_ru: Потеря стоимости капитала от износа и устаревания
options_en: Loss of capital value from wear and obsolescence
questions.explanation_en: Depreciation measures capital stock decline from physical wear and technological obsolescence. Consumer prices, money supply, and exports are separate economic phenomena.

questions.text_en: The accelerator principle suggests that investment depends on:
options: Rate of change in output or sales
options_en: Rate of change in output or sales
questions.explanation_en: The accelerator principle shows investment responds to output growth rates, not absolute levels. Firms invest to meet increased demand, not to match static consumption.

questions.text_en: The relationship between interest rates and investment spending is typically:
questions.explanation_en: Higher interest rates increase borrowing costs, reducing profitable investment projects. Firms face higher financing expenses, discouraging capital expenditure.

questions.text_en: Which of the following best describes the consumption of public goods?
options: Cannot be consumed by multiple people simultaneously
Can be consumed by many people at once without rivalry
Requires individual payment for each unit
options_ru: Не может быть потреблено несколькими людьми одновременно
Может быть потреблено многими людьми одновременно без конкуренции
Требует индивидуального платежа за каждую единицу
options_en: Cannot be consumed by multiple people simultaneously
Can be consumed by many people at once without rivalry
Requires individual payment for each unit
questions.explanation_en: Public goods are non-rivalrous (many can consume simultaneously) and non-excludable (hard to restrict). Defense, roads, and clean air exemplify public consumption patterns.

questions.text_en: Permanent income hypothesis suggests that consumption depends on:
questions.explanation_en: The permanent income hypothesis shows consumption reflects expected long-term income, not temporary fluctuations. Temporary income changes produce minimal consumption effects.

questions.text_en: What prevents all investment funds from flowing to the highest return projects?
options: Risk, information asymmetries, and transaction costs
options_ru: Риск, асимметрия информации и затраты на транзакции
options_en: Risk, information asymmetries, and transaction costs
questions.explanation_en: Market frictions (risk, information gaps, costs) prevent perfect capital allocation. Investors avoid high-risk projects despite potentially high returns.

questions.text_en: The multiplier formula (1/MPS or 1/(1-MPC)) demonstrates that:
options: Lower savings rates produce larger multipliers
options_ru: Более высокие расходы всегда снижают выпуск
Более низкие темпы сбережений производят большие множители
Выпуск никогда не превышает начальные расходы
options_en: Lower savings rates produce larger multipliers
questions.explanation_en: The multiplier is larger when MPS (and thus savings) is smaller, as more income circles through consumption. A large MPC means large multiplier effects.

chapters.title_en: Equilibrium and Proportions of National economy

questions.text_en: National economic equilibrium occurs when which condition is satisfied?
questions.explanation_en: Equilibrium occurs when aggregate supply equals aggregate demand at the equilibrium price level. Excess supply or demand creates pressures toward equilibrium.

questions.text_en: Say's Law of Markets suggests that:
questions.explanation_en: Say's Law posits that production creates purchasing power to demand equal output. This assumes flexible prices and full resource utilization.

questions.text_en: General equilibrium in an economy requires which of the following?
options: Supply exceeds demand in all markets
All markets simultaneously clear at equilibrium prices
Some markets remain in perpetual disequilibrium
Prices remain fixed across all goods
options_ru: Предложение превышает спрос на всех рынках
Все рынки одновременно очищаются в равновесных ценах
Некоторые рынки остаются в вечном неравновесии
Цены остаются фиксированными для всех товаров
options_en: Supply exceeds demand in all markets
All markets simultaneously clear at equilibrium prices
Some markets remain in perpetual disequilibrium
Prices remain fixed across all goods
questions.explanation_en: General equilibrium means all markets clear simultaneously at equilibrium prices. Partial equilibrium examines individual markets in isolation.

questions.text_en: Proportional development in an economy means:
options: Sectors grow at balanced rates maintaining structural proportions
options_ru: Секторы растут сбалансированными темпами, поддерживая структурные пропорции
options_en: Sectors grow at balanced rates maintaining structural proportions
questions.explanation_en: Proportional development means sectors grow maintaining economic balance and structural relationships. Disproportional growth creates imbalances and bottlenecks.

questions.text_en: Which factor imbalance most directly disrupts economic equilibrium?
questions.explanation_en: Labor-capital imbalances create unemployment or capital underutilization, disrupting equilibrium. Proper factor proportions enable efficient, balanced growth.

questions.text_en: Sectoral balance in an economy is important for:
options: Preventing bottlenecks and ensuring sustainable growth
options_ru: Предотвращение узких мест и обеспечение устойчивого роста
options_en: Preventing bottlenecks and ensuring sustainable growth
questions.explanation_en: Sectoral balance prevents supply bottlenecks in critical sectors and enables coordinated growth. Imbalances create shortages in some sectors and excess capacity in others.

questions.text_en: The labor-capital ratio in production refers to:
options: Amount of labor relative to capital input
options_en: Amount of labor relative to capital input
questions.explanation_en: The labor-capital ratio measures production factor proportions, critical for efficiency. It determines output per worker and affects capital productivity.

questions.text_en: Resource allocation efficiency is achieved when:
options: Marginal returns equalize across alternative uses
options_ru: Максимальные ресурсы идут на сельское хозяйство
Предельные возвраты выравниваются в альтернативных использованиях
options_en: Marginal returns equalize across alternative uses
questions.explanation_en: Efficient allocation occurs when marginal returns equalize, so resources moving between uses don't create gains. This maximizes total output from available resources.

questions.text_en: Disproportionate sectoral development creates which problem?
options_ru: Узкие места в недостаточно поставляемых секторах
questions.explanation_en: Disproportionate development creates sectoral bottlenecks where undersupply constrains overall growth. Sectors grow unevenly, creating imbalances and inefficiencies.

questions.text_en: Supply-demand balance in markets is maintained through which mechanism?
options: Price adjustments responding to excess or shortage
options_ru: Корректировки цен в ответ на избыток или дефицит
options_en: Price adjustments responding to excess or shortage
questions.explanation_en: Price signals adjust supply-demand imbalances; excess supply lowers prices, and shortages raise them. This mechanism guides producers and consumers toward equilibrium.

questions.text_en: Macroeconomic balance requires equilibrium between which components?
questions.explanation_en: Macroeconomic balance requires AD=AS at equilibrium price level. This balances all demand components (C, I, G, X-M) with total productive capacity.

questions.text_en: When aggregate demand exceeds aggregate supply, the typical result is:
options_ru: Инфляция и давление цен, вызванные спросом
questions.explanation_en: Excess demand creates demand-pull inflation as buyers bid up prices. Firms may expand output but face supply constraints, pushing prices higher.

questions.text_en: Structural imbalances in an economy typically result from:
questions.explanation_en: Structural imbalances reflect deep sectoral misalignments requiring long-term adjustment. Temporary shocks are cyclical; good factor mobility reduces structural problems.

questions.text_en: Which condition characterizes an economy in disequilibrium?
questions.explanation_en: Disequilibrium manifests as unintended inventory changes—accumulation when demand is weak, depletion when demand exceeds supply. This signals movement toward equilibrium.

questions.text_en: The equilibrium price level in an economy is determined by:
options: Intersection of aggregate demand and supply
options_en: Intersection of aggregate demand and supply
questions.explanation_en: The equilibrium price level emerges where aggregate demand and supply curves intersect. This represents the price at which all markets clear.

questions.text_en: Sectoral ratios measure which relationship in an economy?
options: Proportions of output and employment across sectors
options_ru: Пропорции выпуска и занятости по секторам
options_en: Proportions of output and employment across sectors
questions.explanation_en: Sectoral ratios show how output and employment distribute across primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors. They reveal economic structure and development stage.

questions.text_en: Factor proportions equilibrium requires that:
options: Capital and labor are always unlimited
Returns per factor unit equalize across uses
One factor is always in excess
options_ru: Возвраты за единицу фактора выравниваются в использованиях
Никакие замены не существуют между факторами
options_en: Capital and labor are always unlimited
Returns per factor unit equalize across uses
One factor is always in excess
questions.explanation_en: In factor proportion equilibrium, marginal returns to capital and labor equalize across uses. If not, factors would flow to higher-return uses.

questions.text_en: Economic imbalance between supply capacity and demand creates pressure for:
questions.explanation_en: Supply-demand imbalances trigger adjustment mechanisms—price changes, output changes, and factor reallocation—driving the economy toward new equilibrium.

questions.text_en: In a balanced economic system, the income earned from production must equal:
questions.explanation_en: The income-expenditure identity shows that factor income must equal total spending. This accounting identity holds in equilibrium and is a fundamental national accounting principle.

questions.text_en: Disproportionality in growth means:
options: All sectors grow at identical rates
Sectors grow at vastly different rates creating imbalances
options_ru: Все секторы растут с идентичными темпами
Секторы растут с сильно отличающимися темпами, создавая дисбалансы
options_en: All sectors grow at identical rates
Sectors grow at vastly different rates creating imbalances
questions.explanation_en: Disproportionate growth creates sectoral imbalances—some sectors booming while others stagnate. This creates bottlenecks, unemployment, and misallocated resources.

questions.text_en: Market-clearing in all sectors simultaneously defines:
questions.explanation_en: General equilibrium occurs when all markets clear simultaneously at equilibrium prices. Partial equilibrium examines single markets in isolation.

questions.text_en: Which phenomenon indicates the economy is NOT in equilibrium?
options_ru: Растущая безработица несмотря на рост выпуска
questions.explanation_en: Rising unemployment while output grows indicates structural imbalance—productive capacity not aligned with labor utilization. True equilibrium shows coordinated growth.

questions.text_en: Say's Law fails to hold when:
options: Markets experience rigidities and demand deficiency
options_ru: Рынки испытывают жесткость и недостаточность спроса
options_en: Markets experience rigidities and demand deficiency
questions.explanation_en: Say's Law assumes flexible prices and full employment. When prices are sticky and demand becomes deficient (as in recessions), supply cannot create its own demand.

questions.text_en: Inter-sectoral balance is crucial for preventing:
options_ru: Узкие места и неэффективное распределение ресурсов
questions.explanation_en: Inter-sectoral balance prevents bottlenecks where one sector's capacity constrains others. Imbalances create supply shortages in critical sectors.

questions.text_en: The optimal capital-labor ratio for an economy depends on:
questions.explanation_en: The optimal capital-labor ratio reflects available factors and productive efficiency. Capital-rich economies use higher capital ratios than labor-abundant ones.

questions.text_en: Proportional development requires that growth in factors of production be:
questions.explanation_en: Proportional development coordinates factor growth to maintain productive balance. Ignoring coordination creates shortages of undersupplied factors.

questions.text_en: The paradox of value (why water is cheap while diamonds are expensive) reflects:
questions.explanation_en: The paradox of value shows that marginal utility (not total utility) determines price, and relative scarcity matters. Water is abundant so marginal utility is low.

questions.text_en: Economic equilibrium analysis assumes all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Instant market clearing through price adjustment
options_ru: Мгновенное рыночное очищение через корректировку цены
options_en: Instant market clearing through price adjustment
questions.explanation_en: Equilibrium analysis assumes rationality, price flexibility, and market clearing. It does not assume persistent imbalances are normal; rather, imbalances trigger adjustment.

questions.text_en: Which of the following best describes the peak phase of a business cycle?
options: Qayta tiklash va o'sishning boshlang'ich bosqichi
options_en: Maximum level of economic activity and output
Initial stage of recovery and growth
questions.explanation_en: The peak represents the highest point of economic activity in the business cycle before contraction begins. The other options describe different phases: trough (B), expansion (C), and recession (D).

questions.text_en: Which indicator leads the business cycle by typically turning downward several months before a recession officially begins?
options_en: Number of workers in manufacturing sectors
questions.explanation_en: Leading indicators like new equipment orders turn downward before recessions. Lagging indicators (A, D) follow the cycle, while coincident indicators (C) move simultaneously with economic conditions.

questions.text_en: What is the primary cause of cyclical unemployment during the trough phase of the business cycle?
options: Unda talab kamayishi natijasida ishlab chiqarishning qisqarilishi
Mutaxassislik va ish joylari o'rtasidagi ketma-ketlik
options_ru: Сокращение производства из-за снижения спроса на товары
Несоответствие между квалификацией и рабочими местами
options_en: Large number of people seeking employment opportunities
Reduction in production due to decreased demand for goods
Mismatch between skills and available job positions
questions.explanation_en: Cyclical unemployment results from inadequate aggregate demand reducing production and requiring fewer workers. Options A (frictional), C (structural), and D (structural) describe other unemployment types unrelated to cyclical downturns.

questions.text_en: In the multiplier-accelerator model, what is the relationship between consumption changes and investment decisions?
options: Sarfiy xarajlar o'zgarishi investitsiyada katta o'zgarishlarga olib keladi
Investitsiya va sarfiy xarajlar mustaqil o'zgaradi
Ular har doim bir xil tezlikda o'zgaradi
options_ru: Изменения потребления приводят к большим колебаниям инвестиций
Инвестиции обратно связаны с потребительскими расходами
Инвестиции и потребление изменяются независимо друг от друга
Они всегда меняются с одинаковой скоростью
options_en: Consumption changes amplify investment fluctuations through accelerator effects
Investment is inversely related to consumer expenditure levels
Investment and consumption change independently of each other
They always change at the same rate simultaneously
questions.explanation_en: The accelerator effect shows consumption growth drives larger investment changes; multiplier effect amplifies demand. B contradicts observed relationships, C ignores the accelerator mechanism, and D oversimplifies dynamics.

questions.text_en: Which type of shock is most likely to cause stagflation during the business cycle?
options: Talab shoki natijasida foiz stavkalari o'sishi
Ta'minot shoki (masalan, neft narxi to'satdan o'sishi)
options_ru: Рост процентных ставок в результате шока спроса
Шок предложения (например, внезапный рост цены нефти)
options_en: Rise in interest rates from demand-side shocks
Supply shock (such as sudden oil price increase)
questions.explanation_en: Supply shocks increase prices while reducing output, causing stagflation. Demand shocks typically move inflation and output in the same direction (A), controlled policies smooth cycles (C), and bubbles cause deflation (D).

questions.text_en: What role do inventory cycles play in amplifying business cycle fluctuations?
options: Ular biznes siklini kuchaytiradigan nisbatan kichik rolni o'ynaydi
Ishlab chiqaruvchilar talab kutishini asosida zaxira o'zgartirishadi
options_ru: Они играют незначительную роль в усилении цикла
Производители изменяют запасы на основе ожиданий спроса
Длина инвентарного цикла составляет в среднем 10 лет
options_en: They play a negligible role in amplifying economic cycles
Producers alter inventory based on demand expectations
Inventory changes are linked to export performance
Inventory cycle length averages approximately 10 years
questions.explanation_en: Inventory cycles amplify demand shocks as firms adjust stock levels based on sales expectations, creating cyclical swings. A underestimates the effect, C confuses causality, and D misstates typical inventory cycle length.

questions.text_en: Which of the following is an example of an automatic stabilizer that reduces business cycle volatility?
options_ru: Встроенные пособия по безработице и социальные платежи
options_en: Launch of additional investment projects during recovery
Progressive increase of average tax rate levels
Built-in unemployment benefits and welfare payments
Change in discount rate by central bank
questions.explanation_en: Automatic stabilizers like unemployment insurance reduce spending volatility without policy decisions. A and D require active policy changes (discretionary), while B is neutral to cycles.

questions.text_en: During the expansion phase, what typically happens to business investment and consumer confidence?
options: Ikkalasi ham kamayadi va musbat yo'lga yo'q
Investitsiya o'sadi lekin sarfiy ishonch kamayadi
Ikkalasi ham o'sadi va ekonomik o'sish imkoniyatini taklif qiladi
Sarfiy ishonch o'sadi lekin investitsiya qo'shqoq bo'ladi
options_ru: Оба снижаются и не обещают позитивные результаты
Инвестиции растут, но потребительское доверие падает
Оба растут и предполагают потенциал экономического роста
Потребительское доверие растет, но инвестиции остаются вялыми
options_en: Both decrease and do not promise positive outcomes
Investment increases but consumer confidence declines
Both increase and suggest economic growth potential
Consumer confidence rises but investment remains sluggish
questions.explanation_en: During expansion, rising business confidence, profits, and consumer optimism drive both investment and spending growth. A describes recession, B shows conflicting signals, and D contradicts observed expansion dynamics.

questions.text_en: What is a depression in economic terminology?
options: Jiddiy va uzoq davom etadigan iqtisodiy qisqarilishi
options_ru: Экономический спад в течение двух-трех лет в среднем
Внезапная рецессия в одном промышленном секторе
options_en: Severe and prolonged economic contraction period
Economic downturn lasting two to three years on average
Sudden recession in a single industrial sector
questions.explanation_en: A depression is a severe, extended contraction with major output and employment losses. A describes mild recessions, C confuses typical cycle lengths, and D describes sectoral downturns.

questions.text_en: Which coincident indicator moves simultaneously with the business cycle turning points?
options: Tanlangan ishchilar soni va ishlab chiqarish indeksi
Sotib olish buyurtmalari va yangi qurilish ruxsatnomasi
Mehmon talabi va turizm tartibsiz o'zgarishi
options_ru: Количество занятых и индекс промышленного производства
Покупаемые заказы и разрешения на новое строительство
Спрос туристов и нестабильные колебания туризма
options_en: New jobs created in manufacturing sector
Number of employed persons and industrial production index
Purchased orders and new construction permits issued
Tourist demand and tourism sector fluctuations
questions.explanation_en: Coincident indicators like employment and production move with the cycle simultaneously. A is a lagging indicator, C are leading indicators, and D reflects sector-specific rather than economy-wide cycles.

questions.text_en: In business cycle analysis, what is the natural rate of output?
options: O'rtacha yillik ishlab chiqarish o'sish tezligi
To'liq bandlik sharoitida potensial ishlab chiqarish darajasi
options_ru: Уровень потенциального выпуска при полной занятости
options_en: Average annual production growth rate achieved
Potential output level at full employment condition
questions.explanation_en: Natural output represents the economy's sustainable production at full employment with stable inflation. A is growth rate, C is arbitrary minimum, and D exceeds sustainable levels.

questions.text_en: What distinguishes a boom from a normal expansion in the business cycle?
options: Boom ishlab chiqarishning kichik o'zgarishini anglatadi
Boom o'rtacha ishlab chiqarishning tez o'sishini ifodalaydi
Boom va expansion bir xil ekonomik bosqichi
Boom faqat ishlab chiqarish sohasida sodir bo'ladi
options_ru: Бум представляет ускоренный рост выпуска выше среднего
Бум и экспансия - одна и та же экономическая фаза
Бум происходит только в производственном секторе
options_en: Boom means small production changes occur
Boom represents accelerated output growth above average
Boom and expansion are the same economic phase
Boom occurs exclusively in manufacturing sector
questions.explanation_en: A boom is stronger, faster expansion with rapid output and employment growth beyond normal rates. A confuses boom with stagnation, C conflates terms, and D ignores economy-wide scope.

questions.text_en: How do demand shocks differ from supply shocks in their effect on inflation and output?
options: Talab shoki inflation va ishlab chiqarishni bir tomonga harakat qiladi
Ta'minot shoki inflation va ishlab chiqarishni qarama-qarshi yo'nalishga harakat qiladi
Ikkalasi ham bir xil ta'siri mavjud
options_ru: Шок спроса движет инфляцию и выпуск в одном направлении
Шок предложения движет инфляцию и выпуск в противоположных направлениях
Оба имеют одинаковое влияние на экономику
Шок спроса не влияет на инфляцию
options_en: Demand shocks move inflation and output in same direction together
Supply shocks move inflation and output in opposite directions
Both shocks produce identical economic effects
Demand shocks do not affect inflation rates
questions.explanation_en: Supply shocks increase prices while reducing output (stagflation), whereas demand shocks move inflation and output together. A mischaracterizes demand shocks, C ignores differences, and D misses demand inflation links.

questions.text_en: What is the typical duration of a business cycle from trough to peak to trough?
options: Hech qanday aniq vaqt yo'q, bu o'zgaruvchan
options_ru: В среднем длится от 2 до 8 лет
options_en: No fixed period exists, it varies
questions.explanation_en: Business cycles typically last 2-8 years, though lengths vary by country and era. A greatly underestimates duration, C overestimates typical length, and D, while true about variation, ignores the observed range.

questions.text_en: Which of the following best represents the relationship between cyclical and frictional unemployment?
options: Ikkalasi ham biznes siklining xuddi shunday bosqichida sodir bo'ladi
Tsiklik ishsizlik biznes siklga bog'liq, friktsional ishsizlik doimiy
Friktsional ishsizlik biznes siklga bog'liq, tsiklik ishsizlik doimiy
Ularni farqlab bo'lmaydi, ularni bir xil narsadir
options_ru: Оба происходят на одной и той же стадии цикла бизнеса
Циклическая безработица связана с циклом, фрикционная постоянна
Фрикционная безработица связана с циклом, циклическая постоянна
Их невозможно отличить, это одна и та же вещь
options_en: Both occur at the same business cycle phase
Cyclical unemployment is cycle-dependent; frictional unemployment is constant
Frictional unemployment cycle-dependent; cyclical unemployment is constant
They cannot be distinguished; they are the same thing
questions.explanation_en: Cyclical unemployment varies with the business cycle, while frictional unemployment (job search) persists regardless of cycle. A ignores timing differences, C reverses the relationship, and D conflates distinct types.

questions.text_en: What does the business cycle's 'trough' indicate about future economic prospects?
options: Iqtisodiy sharoitlar shunga o'xshashligicha yomon bo'ladi
Pincode o'sish boshlangan yoki yaqin orada boshlang'ich
options_ru: Экономические условия останутся столь же плохими
Начался рост или начнется в ближайшее время
options_en: Economic conditions will remain equally poor
Growth has begun or will begin soon thereafter
Market remains in complete stagnation state
questions.explanation_en: The trough marks the bottom of the recession, signaling imminent expansion and recovery. A ignores trough definition, C contradicts cycle mechanics, and D misses that troughs precede recovery.

questions.text_en: How does fiscal policy attempt to stabilize the business cycle?
options: Soliq va sarfalarni ekonomik sharoitga moslashib
options_ru: Адаптируя налоги и расходы к экономическим условиям
options_en: Changing the central bank discount rate levels
Adapting taxes and spending to economic conditions
questions.explanation_en: Fiscal policy uses government spending and tax changes to counter cyclical swings. A describes monetary policy, C is indirect, and D confuses currency dynamics.

questions.text_en: Which phase of the business cycle is characterized by falling incomes and job losses?
questions.explanation_en: Recession involves falling output, income, and rising unemployment as firms reduce operations. A describes expansion opposite characteristics, C marks turning points without contraction, and D marks recovery start.

questions.text_en: What role does the accelerator principle play in amplifying business cycle fluctuations?
options: Bu to'liq samarali emas va siklga ta'sir qilmaydi
Talab o'zgarishlari investitsiya o'zgarishlarida kattaroq o'zgarishga olib keladi
Talab va investitsiya hech qachon o'zaro bog'lanish yok
options_ru: Это совершенно неэффективно и не влияет на цикл
Изменения спроса приводят к больших сменам инвестиций
Спрос и инвестиции никогда не связаны
options_en: This is completely ineffective and affects no cycles
Demand changes cause larger swings in investment
Investment always remains at constant levels
Demand and investment are never related
questions.explanation_en: The accelerator shows small demand changes trigger larger investment swings, amplifying cycles. A denies the effect, C assumes constant investment ignoring demand responsiveness, and D ignores business reality.

questions.text_en: During a crisis phase, what typically happens to credit availability and borrowing costs?
options: Kredit oshadi va foiz stavkalari tushadi
Kredit qisqaradi va foiz stavkalari ko'tariladi
Foiz stavkalari tushadi lekin kredit oshadi
options_ru: Кредит расширяется и процентные ставки падают
Кредит сужается и процентные ставки растут
Кредит и процентные ставки не меняются
Процентные ставки падают, но кредит расширяется
options_en: Credit expands and interest rates decrease
Credit contracts and interest rates increase
Credit and interest rates remain unchanged
Interest rates fall but credit expands
questions.explanation_en: During financial crises, credit freezes as banks become risk-averse, driving up borrowing costs. A describes expansion conditions, C ignores crisis dynamics, and D contradicts observed credit squeeze patterns.

questions.text_en: What is the relationship between the output gap and the business cycle?
options: Yo'qligi hech qachon nol o'zgaradi va tsiklga ta'sir qilmaydi
Gap musbat bilan o'sish, manfiy bilan kontraksiya ko'rsatadi
Gap har doim nolga teng bo'ladi
Gap va tsikl o'zaro bog'lanish yok
options_ru: Разрыв никогда не меняется и не влияет на цикл
Положительный разрыв указывает на рост, отрицательный на сокращение
Разрыв и цикл никогда не связаны
options_en: Gap never changes and affects no cycles
Positive gap indicates growth, negative gap indicates contraction
Gap is always equal to zero
Gap and cycle are never related
questions.explanation_en: The output gap (actual minus potential output) widens during booms (positive) and shrinks during recessions (negative), tracking the cycle. A denies variation, C assumes zero gap always, and D ignores their direct relationship.

questions.text_en: How do leading indicators help predict future economic downturns?
options: Ular aslo hech qanday bashorat berish qobiliyatiga ega emas
Ular retsessiya old ma'lumotlar beradi ularni tayyorlashga imkon beradi
Ular retsessiya boshlanganidan keyin sodir bo'ladi
Ularning hech qanday iqtisodiy ahamiyati yo'q
options_ru: Они вообще не имеют способности предсказывать
Они дают ранние признаки рецессии, позволяя подготовиться
Они не имеют никакого экономического значения
options_en: They have no predictive capability whatsoever
They provide early recession signals enabling preparation
They occur after recessions have already begun
questions.explanation_en: Leading indicators turn before cycles, allowing policymakers to act preemptively. A denies their predictive value, C describes coincident/lagging indicators, and D contradicts empirical evidence.

questions.text_en: What does monetary policy accomplish through open market operations during a recession?
options: Markaziy bank qimmatli qog'ozlarni sotib oladi va pul quyadi
Markaziy bank qimmatli qog'ozlarni sotadi va pul chiqaradi
Markaziy bank o'ziga hech narsani yo'k qiladi
options_ru: Центральный банк покупает ценные бумаги и вводит деньги
Центральный банк продает ценные бумаги и забирает деньги
options_en: Central bank buys securities and injects money
Central bank sells securities and withdraws money
Central bank has no available tools
questions.explanation_en: During recessions, central banks conduct open market operations buying securities to increase money supply and lower interest rates. B contradicts recession policy goals, C and D deny central bank's stabilization role.

questions.text_en: Which of the following best characterizes the relationship between capacity utilization and the business cycle?
options: Qabul ishlatilishi biznes siklga bog'lanish yo'q
Qabul ishlatilishi ekspansion davri o'sadi, retsessiyada kamayadi
Qabul ishlatilishi har doim 100 foizda turadi
Qabul ishlatilishi sodir bo'layotgan narsaga ta'sir qilmaydi
options_ru: Использование мощности не связано с деловым циклом
Использование мощности растет в период расширения и падает в рецессии
Использование мощности всегда находится на уровне 100 процентов
Использование мощности не влияет на то, что происходит
options_en: Capacity utilization is unrelated to business cycle
Capacity utilization rises during expansion and falls in recession
Capacity utilization always stays at 100 percent
Capacity utilization does not impact economic activity
questions.explanation_en: Capacity utilization rises as output increases during expansions and falls during contractions. A denies cyclical relationship, C assumes full utilization always (unrealistic), and D ignores its role.

questions.text_en: How do asset price bubbles relate to business cycle dynamics and crises?
options: Ular retsessiyaga hech qanday ta'sir qilmaydi
Ular jo'shmalarni qo'zg'atadi va buziladigan vaqtda krizis keltirib chiqaradi
Ular doimi tizimda ijobiy ta'sir qiladi
Ular faqat fondga bozorida sodir bo'ladi va boshqalar emas
options_ru: Они никак не влияют на рецессию
Они стимулируют бум и вызывают кризис, когда лопаются
Они всегда оказывают положительное влияние на систему
Они происходят только на фондовом рынке и больше нигде
options_en: They have no impact on recessions
They fuel booms and trigger crises when they burst
They always exert positive system effects
They occur only in stock markets and nowhere else
questions.explanation_en: Asset bubbles amplify booms with unsustainable asset prices and cause crises when bursting, as in 2008. A ignores financial crisis links, C denies boom-bust instability, and D ignores real estate and other bubbles.

questions.text_en: What effect does the multiplier have on initial demand shocks in the business cycle?
options: U shoki kuchaytirib, dastlabki ta'sirdan kattaroq joriy ta'sirni keltirib chiqaradi
U shoki zaifalab, dastlabki ta'sirdan kichikroq jami ta'sirni keltirib chiqaradi
U hech qanday ta'sirga ega emas
U shoki yo'q qiladi va ta'sir qilmaydi
options_ru: Он усиливает шок, создавая больший совокупный эффект чем начальный удар
Он ослабляет шок, создавая меньший совокупный эффект
Он устраняет шок и не влияет
options_en: It amplifies the shock, creating larger aggregate effects than initial impact
It weakens the shock, creating smaller total effects
It has no effect on shocks
It eliminates shocks and prevents impacts
questions.explanation_en: The multiplier amplifies initial demand changes through rounds of spending and income, magnifying cycle effects. B contradicts multiplier mechanics, C and D deny multiplier existence and functionality.

questions.text_en: Which of the following best describes the procyclical nature of private investment?
options: Investitsiya har doim doimiy darajada turadi
Investitsiya ekspansion davri o'sadi, kontraksiyada kamayadi
options_ru: Инвестиции всегда остаются на постоянном уровне
Инвестиции растут во время расширения и падают во время сокращения
Инвестиции растут во время рецессии и падают во время расширения
Инвестиции не связаны с деловым циклом
options_en: Investment always remains at constant levels
Investment grows during expansion and falls during contraction
Investment rises during recession and falls during expansion
Investment is unrelated to business cycle
questions.explanation_en: Private investment is procyclical, moving with the cycle due to profit expectations and cash flow. A ignores cyclical variation, C reverses the relationship, and D denies observable correlation.

questions.text_en: What is the primary mechanism through which demand shocks propagate through the economy in business cycles?
options: Ishlab chiqarish tezligi subratsion shaklida o'zgarmaydi
Talab o'zgarishi ishlab chiqarish va daromadga ta'sir qiladi va shunga bo'lib sarfiy xarajlar
Talab hech qachon ishlab chiqarishga ta'sir qilmaydi
Ishlab chiqarish erkli o'zgaradi va talab uni kuzatadi
options_ru: Скорость производства не меняется в виде вычитания
Изменение спроса влияет на выпуск и доход, а затем на потребительские расходы
Спрос никогда не влияет на выпуск
Выпуск изменяется независимо, и спрос следует за ним
options_en: Production speed does not change in subtraction form
Demand change affects output and income, then consumer spending
Output changes independently and demand follows
questions.explanation_en: Demand shocks trigger output changes, which alter incomes, which shift consumption and investment, propagating effects through multipliers. A is unintelligible, C and D deny demand-side mechanisms.

questions.text_en: How do expectations of future economic conditions affect current business cycle dynamics?
options: Kutish hech qanday roli yo'q, faqat hozirgi sharoitlar ahamiyatli
Ehtimol o'sish kutishi investitsiya va sarfiy xarajlarni joriy oshiradi
Kutish haqida nima bo'lmasin, hozirgi shartnomada ta'sir qilmaydi
Kundalik yo'l boshqa kutishlarga bog'liq emas
options_ru: Ожидания не имеют роли, важны только текущие условия
Ожидание вероятного роста стимулирует текущие инвестиции и потребление
Ожидания ничего, не влияют на текущие условия
Ежедневные операции не зависят от других ожиданий
options_en: Expectations have no role; only current conditions matter
Expected future growth stimulates current investment and consumption
Expectations have no effect on current conditions
Daily operations are independent of other expectations
questions.explanation_en: Future expectations shape current spending and investment decisions through forward-looking behavior, affecting immediate cycle dynamics. A and C deny forward-looking economic behavior, while D ignores decision-making linkages.

questions.text_en: What distinguishes a financial crisis from a standard business cycle recession?
options: Ularning o'rtasida hech qanday farq yo'q
Krizis kredit tizimini buzadi va daimiy rivojlanmoqda
Krizis ularni ushbu juda o'z-o'ziga qaytaradi
options_ru: Кризис разрушает кредитную систему и вызывает самоусиление спирали
Кризис просто это же самое с другим названием
Рецессия более серьезна, кризис менее серьезен
options_en: There is no difference between them
Crisis disrupts credit system and creates self-reinforcing downturn spiral
Crisis is the same thing with another name
Recession is more severe; crisis is less severe
questions.explanation_en: Financial crises disrupt credit intermediation causing deeper, self-perpetuating contractions beyond normal cyclical recessions. A denies distinctness, C equates different phenomena, and D reverses severity relationship.

questions.text_en: Which of the following is included in the labor force?
options: Ish qidirayotgan ishchi va bandlik o'tkazgan odam
options_ru: Безработные, ищущие работу и занятые люди
options_en: Unemployed seeking work and employed persons
Employed individuals and those seeking employment
questions.explanation_en: The labor force includes employed persons and unemployed individuals actively seeking work. A includes wrong categories, C excludes unemployed, and D includes out-of-labor-force populations.

questions.text_en: How is the labor force participation rate calculated?
options: Ish bazasidagi shaxslarning ish yoshidagi aholiga nisbati
Faqat ish qilidiganlaring ish yoshidagi aholisiga nisbati
options_ru: Отношение рабочей силы к рабочему возрастному населению
Отношение только занятых к рабочему возрасту
options_en: Ratio of unemployed to employed workers
Ratio of labor force to working-age population
Ratio of only employed to working-age population
questions.explanation_en: Labor force participation rate = (Labor force / Working-age population) × 100. A confuses unemployment ratio, C omits unemployed from numerator, and D measures intensity rather than participation.

questions.text_en: What is the unemployment rate?
options: Ish bazasidagi shaxslarning ish yoshidagi aholisiga nisbati
options_ru: Отношение рабочей силы к рабочему возрасту
options_en: Ratio of unemployed to total labor force
Ratio of labor force to working-age population
questions.explanation_en: Unemployment rate = (Unemployed / Labor force) × 100. A uses wrong denominator, C calculates participation rate instead, and D measures employment not unemployment.

questions.text_en: What is structural unemployment?
options: Ish va ishchi o'rtasida mutaxassislik ketma-ketligi
options_ru: Несоответствие между требуемыми навыками и доступными рабочими местами
options_en: Seasonal unemployment from periodic job loss
Mismatch between required skills and available jobs
Arises from changes in nature of work
questions.explanation_en: Structural unemployment results from skill mismatches, industry shifts, or geographic imbalances. A describes seasonal, C and D describe cyclical or frictional unemployment causes.

questions.text_en: Which type of unemployment is mainly due to the time required to search for a suitable job?
options_en: Frictional unemployment from job search time
questions.explanation_en: Frictional unemployment occurs as workers search for jobs matching their skills and preferences. A addresses skill mismatches, C addresses demand deficiency, and D is not a standard unemployment type.

questions.text_en: What does NAIRU represent in labor economics?
options: Eng kichik yaladlarning tomonidan takhmin qilingan ish qo'rg'anitligi
Ishsizlik stavkasi inflatsiyani tezlashtirasiga sabab bo'lmaydigan
options_ru: Уровень безработицы, который не вызывает ускорение инфляции
options_en: Unemployment rate that does not cause inflation acceleration
questions.explanation_en: NAIRU (Non-Accelerating Inflation Rate of Unemployment) is the unemployment level compatible with stable inflation. A uses wrong methodology, C confuses direction, and D measures employment quantity.

questions.text_en: What is the natural rate of unemployment?
options: NAIRU da ekvivalent, friktsion va strukturaviy ishsizlikning yig'indisi
Eng kichik mumkin bo'lgan ishsizlik darajasi
options_ru: Эквивалент NAIRU, сумма фрикционной и структурной безработицы
options_en: NAIRU equivalent, sum of frictional and structural unemployment
questions.explanation_en: The natural rate of unemployment consists of frictional and structural unemployment, roughly equivalent to NAIRU. B ignores structural unemployment existence, C confuses measurement types, and D is economically impossible.

questions.text_en: How does human capital affect labor market outcomes?
options: Inson kapitali hech qanday ta'sir qilmaydi
Yuksharoq ta'lim va ko'nikmalari yuqori daromad va bandlik imkoniyatini beradi
Inson kapitali faqat sining boshidagi o'lchami
Inson kapitali bandlik qilishdan to'sip qo'yadi
options_ru: Более высокое образование и навыки дают лучший доход и возможности
Человеческий капитал - это только размер ума
options_en: Human capital has no impact on outcomes
Higher education and skills provide better income and opportunities
Human capital is only brain size measurement
questions.explanation_en: Human capital (education, skills, experience) increases earning potential and employment opportunities. A denies its importance, C confuses physical with human capital, and D contradicts empirical evidence.

questions.text_en: What is labor productivity?
options: Har bir ishchi tomonidan vaqt birligida ishlab chiqarilgan mahsulot
options_ru: Выпуск, производимый каждым работником за единицу времени
options_en: Multiplying number of workers and employment
Output produced by each worker per unit time
Number of job locations for employed workers
questions.explanation_en: Labor productivity measures output per worker per time period. A confuses aggregation, C measures job availability, and D denies fundamental economic concept.

questions.text_en: What effect does skill mismatch have on the labor market?
options: Ishchinlarni o'z ko'nikmalaridan ko'ra juda pastroq maosh bilan ish topishiga sabab bo'ladi
Juda yuksharoq ish topish imkoni beradi
options_ru: Приводит к поиску работы ниже квалификации и более низкого заработка
options_en: No effect on labor market outcomes
Leads to underemployment and lower wages for workers
questions.explanation_en: Skill mismatches lead workers to accept positions below their qualifications at lower pay. A ignores documented effects, C overstates impact, and D contradicts mismatch consequences.

questions.text_en: How do geographic factors affect labor mobility?
options: Uzoq masofalar va ko'chirishni o'rnashtirishning xaraji ishchilarni boshqa joyga ko'chishni to'sip qo'yadi
Hamma joyda o'xshash ish imkoni mavjud
Bandlik doimi bir xil joyda bo'ladi
options_ru: Дальние расстояния и расходы на переезд препятствуют мобильности рабочих
Занятость всегда остается в одном месте
options_en: Long distances and relocation costs limit worker geographic mobility
Employment always remains in one location
questions.explanation_en: Geographic mobility is limited by relocation costs and distance, affecting labor market adjustments. A denies geographic constraints, C assumes uniform opportunities, and D ignores mobility possibility.

questions.text_en: What is the relationship between wage dynamics and labor supply?
options: Maosh o'zgarishi ish bozorida ta'sir qilmaydi
Yuqori maosh ish taklifi ko'paytirib, pastroq maosh kamaytirib
Maosh va ish taklifi teskari bog'langan
options_ru: Изменения зарплаты не влияют на рынок труда
Более высокая зарплата увеличивает предложение труда, более низкая снижает
Зарплата и предложение труда обратно пропорциональны
Предложение труда независимо от изменений зарплаты
options_en: Wage changes have no impact on labor market
Higher wages increase labor supply; lower wages decrease it
Wages and labor supply are inversely proportional
Labor supply is independent of wage changes
questions.explanation_en: Higher wages encourage more labor supply (substitution effect dominates), attracting more workers. A denies labor supply responsiveness, C reverses relationship, and D assumes wage inelasticity.

questions.text_en: What occurs when labor demand exceeds labor supply?
options: Ish bozorida kamboyli holat, maosh ko'tariladi
options_en: Tight labor market with rising wages
questions.explanation_en: When labor demand exceeds supply, employers compete for workers, driving wages up. A describes labor surplus, C contradicts scarcity dynamics, and D ignores market mechanisms.

questions.text_en: What is job creation?
options: Yangi ish o'rinlari shuning ortida ishlab chiqarish yoki xizmatlar tayyorlash
options_ru: Создание новых рабочих мест путем производства или услуг
options_en: Number of jobs lost by workers
Creation of new jobs through production or services
questions.explanation_en: Job creation refers to new employment positions generated through economic expansion. A describes job destruction, C measures unemployment, and D quantifies only a subset.

questions.text_en: What is job destruction?
options: Bandlikni o'tkazib yuborilishi va ish o'rinlarining yo'q bo'lishi
options_ru: Потеря занятости и исчезновение рабочих мест
options_en: Loss of employment and disappearance of jobs
Increase in number of job seekers
questions.explanation_en: Job destruction occurs when businesses eliminate positions through closures or reductions. A describes opposite phenomenon, C measures unemployment consequences, and D limits scope incorrectly.

questions.text_en: How does labor force participation vary across demographic groups?
options: Jinsiy, yoshlik va ta'lim darajasiga bog'liq
options_ru: Зависит от пола, возраста и уровня образования
options_en: Depends on gender, age and education level
questions.explanation_en: Labor force participation varies significantly by gender, age, education, and other demographics. A assumes uniformity inconsistent with data, C omits gender and age differences, and D is irrelevant.

questions.text_en: What is the relationship between education and employment prospects?
options: Yuqori ta'lim o'rtacha yuqori maosh va kamroq ishsizlik beradi
O'rta ta'lim eng yaxshi natija beradi
options_ru: Более высокое образование обычно дает более высокие зарплаты и ниже безработицу
options_en: Education has no impact on prospects
Higher education usually offers better wages and lower unemployment
questions.explanation_en: Higher education correlates with higher earnings and lower unemployment rates. A denies education-employment link, C contradicts evidence, and D understates higher education benefits.

questions.text_en: What is labor supply elasticity?
options: Maosh o'zgarishiga ish taklifi qanchalik javob beradi
Ish talabi faqat nol foizga o'zgaradi
options_ru: Чувствительность предложения труда к изменению зарплаты
Спрос на труд меняется только на ноль процентов
options_en: Sensitivity of labor supply to wage changes
Labor demand changes only by zero percent
questions.explanation_en: Labor supply elasticity measures how much labor quantity supplied responds to wage changes. A assumes no variation, C assumes wage constancy, and D confuses quantity response metrics.

questions.text_en: What happens to labor demand when firms' output increases?
options: Ishchilar sonini ko'paytirib, ish talabi o'sadi
options_ru: Спрос на труд растет для производства большего объема
options_en: Labor demand increases to produce higher output volume
questions.explanation_en: Increased output requires more workers, so labor demand rises as firms expand production. A contradicts output-employment relationship, C ignores production requirements, and D confuses wage determination.

questions.text_en: What is underemployment in the labor market?
options: Ishchilar ko'nikmalaridan pastroq darajada ish qiladi yoki ish vaqti qisqa
options_ru: Работники занимают должности ниже их навыков или работают неполный рабочий день
options_en: Absence of work, similar to unemployment
Workers in positions below their skills or working part-time
questions.explanation_en: Underemployment occurs when skilled workers take lower-skill jobs or work fewer hours than desired. A confuses with unemployment, C describes labor surplus conditions, and D denies the concept.

questions.text_en: How does technological change affect labor markets?
options: Ba'zi ish o'rinlari yo'q bo'ladi lekin yangi ko'nikma talabi va yangi ish o'rinlari kelib chiqadi
Faqat jadval ishlab chiqarishning yo'q bo'ladi
options_ru: Некоторые рабочие места исчезают, но возникает спрос на новые навыки и новые должности
options_en: Has no impact on labor markets
Some jobs disappear but new skill demands and positions emerge
All jobs remain exactly the same
questions.explanation_en: Technology eliminates some jobs while creating new opportunities requiring different skills. A denies technological impact, C understates breadth of change, and D ignores economic restructuring.

questions.text_en: What is the difference between nominal and real wages?
options: Ularning o'rtasida hech qanday farq yo'q
Nominallik pul miqdori, haqiqiy narxlar nisbatiga to'g'rilangan
